benchmark_type_evidence: We introduce MAKIEVAL, an automatic multilingual framework for evaluating cultural awareness in LLMs across languages, regions, and topics.
brief_description: MAKIEVAL is an automatic multilingual framework for evaluating cultural awareness in LLMs through open-ended text generation, leveraging Wikidata as a cross-lingual anchor to extract and link cultural entities without translation. It evaluates 7 LLMs across 13 languages, 19 countries/regions, and 6 culturally salient topics using four metrics: granularity, diversity, culture specificity, and culture consensus.

datasets.task_type: open-ended text generation for cultural awareness evaluation
datasets.annotation_method: Prompt templates designed by researchers and validated by 15 native speakers (at least one per language). Entity extraction from model outputs performed automatically by GPT-4o-mini. Entity linking to Wikidata is fully automatic. Manual evaluation of extraction quality conducted by native speakers on sampled data (50 sentences × 6 topics × 4 languages).

data_creator_info.creator_affiliation: MaiNLP, Center for Information and Language Processing, LMU Munich; Munich Center for Machine Learning (MCML)
data_creator_info.evidence: 15 native speakers participated in prompt validation (at least one per language). Native speakers who validated prompts and annotated extraction quality include speakers of German, Spanish (Spain & Mexico), English (American & British), Turkish, Persian, Arabic, Hindi, Japanese, Korean, Traditional Chinese (Taiwan), Thai, Chinese (Mainland), and Italian. All annotators were native speakers with graduate-level education background.

datasets.notes: MAKIEVAL is a framework rather than a static benchmark. It uses template-based prompts (Neutral, Explicit, Implicit) across 6 topics (food, beverages, clothing, books, music, transportation) and 19 countries/regions. Each prompt generates 500 responses per model. Total: 1,716 unique prompts, over 85.8 million generated texts across 7 evaluated models, 24,042 matched Wikidata cultural entities. Hausa and Yoruba were explored but excluded due to poor generation quality from open-source models.

translated.evidence: The prompt templates are parallel constructions across 13 languages (structurally equivalent templates). However, 'we invited native speakers to review and validate the prompts. A total of 15 native speakers participated in this validation process, with at least one annotator per language.' The evaluation methodology itself avoids translation entirely, using Wikidata as a cross-lingual anchor: 'enabling scalable, language-agnostic evaluation without manual annotation or translation.'

native_annotators.evidence: 15 native speakers validated prompt templates (at least one per language). Manual evaluation of entity extraction was done by native speakers with graduate-level education (one per language for Arabic, Chinese, English, Hindi; later extended to 13 languages in Table 8). However, the core entity extraction is automated via GPT-4o-mini, not manual native annotation.

culturally_grounded.evidence: The entire framework is designed to evaluate cultural awareness. Prompts reference 19 specific countries/regions across 6 culturally salient topics (food, beverages, clothing, books, music, transportation). Evaluation metrics include Culture Specificity (whether entities are aligned with the target culture) and Culture Consensus (cross-lingual agreement). The paper states: 'MAKIEVAL evaluates open-ended text generation, capturing how models express culturally grounded knowledge in natural language.'

MAKIEVAL.annotation_quality_notes: Entity extraction by GPT-4o-mini was manually evaluated across 13 languages with F1 scores ranging from 90.38% (Persian) to 96.50% (German). Domain-specific F1 ranges from 91.4% (Beverages) to 97.4% (Books). Wikidata matching has 26-36% missing QIDs per topic, partly due to model hallucination of non-existent entities. The framework includes disambiguation procedures for ambiguous Wikidata labels.

datasets_from_scratch_no_english_source.evidence: The prompt templates are parallel constructions across 13 languages based on a shared structural format (shown in Table 7/Figure 7). While each language version was validated by native speakers, the template design follows a common English-originated structure. The evaluation methodology (Wikidata-based entity matching) is language-agnostic and not derived from English.

datasets_translated_from_english.evidence: The prompt templates follow parallel structures across all 13 languages, originating from a shared template design (see Table 1 and Figure 7). Templates were then validated by 15 native speakers. However, the evaluation framework itself explicitly avoids translation: 'enabling scalable, language-agnostic evaluation without manual annotation or translation.'

details.MAKIEVAL: The framework is specifically designed to evaluate cultural awareness. It covers 19 countries/regions across 6 culturally salient topics (food, beverages, clothing, books, music, transportation). Metrics include Culture Specificity (proportion of entities linked to target culture) and Culture Consensus (cross-lingual entity overlap). Prompts include explicit cultural contextualization (country names) and implicit cues (culturally associated names).

all_annotators_native_speakers.value: yes, for prompt validation; automatic for entity extraction

Languages covered: German, Spanish (Spain & Mexico), English (American & British), Turkish, Persian, Arabic, Hindi, Japanese, Korean, Traditional Chinese (Taiwan), Thai, Chinese (Mainland), Italian. Entity extraction quality was manually evaluated by native speakers with graduate-level education. Core entity extraction is automated via GPT-4o-mini.

affiliations: MaiNLP, Center for Information and Language Processing, LMU Munich
annotator_workforce.evidence: A total of 15 native speakers participated in prompt validation. The paper does not report annotator compensation or IRB/ethics review. The Ethical Concern section states: 'We do not foresee any ethical concerns associated with this work. All analyses were conducted using publicly available models. No private or sensitive information was used.' Research was supported by ERC Consolidator Grant DIALECT 101043235 and an OpenAI compute grant.

cultural_flags.english_centricity_notes: The paper explicitly identifies and measures English-centricity as a key finding: 'English prompts consistently achieve the highest specificity gains when adding cultural context across nearly all countries and models. This suggests that LLMs are more sensitive to cultural signals in English, likely due to the disproportionate amount of English data in their pretraining corpora.' The framework is designed to detect and quantify this English bias, rather than being English-centric itself. Prompts are parallel template constructions but the evaluation uses Wikidata as a language-agnostic bridge.

notably_excluded: Sub-Saharan Africa (Hausa and Yoruba explored but excluded due to poor model generation quality)
geographic_representation.evidence: 19 countries/regions across 8 geographic areas (East Asia, South Asia, Middle East, Europe, North America, Latin America, Australia, Africa). Africa represented only by Nigeria (English-speaking). The paper notes: 'we initially explored two low-resource African languages: Hausa and Yoruba. However... we found that open-source models produced text of very poor quality in these two languages.'
